verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Change of clock only. The paper measures y from the start of each stage (p.129: a local coordinate with 'origin at the start of the stage'); the Lean file uses one global log-radius clock whose first ramp starts at 0 (module doc), so this stage is 1 ≤ y_glob ≤ 1 + dropLength and y_glob = 1 + y_loc. Then Real.log y_glob = log(1 + y_loc), so dropCoefficient c.m y_glob = 4[1 - σ(log(1+y_loc)/M_d)] = k(y_loc) with m = M_d; dropCoefficient_eq proves the `if y ≤ 1 then 4` branch is that same formula for all y > 0, i.e. a flat extension to the left of the stage. dropLength = exp m + 10 is literally the paper's T_d of (A.6), so the stage length matches and k vanishes on the last eleven units of it (dropCoefficient_late, line 236, gives 0 for y_glob ≥ e^m, i.e. y_loc ≥ e^{M_d} - 1). l = 0 on the stage is slope_drop and U = k(y)η is initialAxial / axial_before_pulse. One packaging point: the Lean's dropCoefficient is a total function of y, so the restriction 0 ≤ y ≤ T_d appears only through the interval hypotheses of slope_drop and of the lemmas that use it, not as a domain of k.
